results.content:
Title: Scalability vs Performance
# Scalability vs Performance. # Scalability vs Performance. In system design, **Scalability** and **Performance** are often confused, mixed, or used interchangeably. *   A fast system is scalable. *   A scalable system is fast. > **_When should we optimize for performance, and when should we design for scalability? ### Performance. ### Scalability. ## 5️⃣ What is Scalability? A system is **scalable** if:. Increasing performance in general means serving more units of work, but it can also be to handle larger units of work, such as when datasets grow. 👉 A scalable system ensures that **adding redundancy does NOT reduce performance**. This graph shows **how performance changes as load increases** for a **poorly scalable system**. > **_Good performance at low load does NOT mean the system is scalable._**. > **_Scalability is about protecting performance at high scale, not optimizing low scale._**. > **_Scalability is about keeping performance stable as load grows._**. > _“A scalable system maintains roughly constant performance as load increases, even if that means slightly lower performance at low load.”_. > The blue curve represents a system optimized only for performance, which collapses as traffic grows. The orange line represents a system designed for scalability, where performance remains stable even under heavy load. ## 7️⃣ Why scalability is so hard. > **_First make it scalable, then make it fast._**. *   Performance and scalability are **not the same**. *   Scalability must be **designed**, not patched. ## 9️⃣ How Google Balances Performance and Scalability. Google never treats performance and scalability as opposing choices. *   Design systems that can **scale horizontally** by adding more machines. > **_Google designs systems to survive success first —_**. This mindset is why Google products continue to perform well even as they grow to serve billions of users worldwide. *   Start by designing for **scalability**. > _“Performance is about optimizing individual requests, while scalability is about ensuring the system continues to perform as demand grows.”_. ## How Uber Built a System That Never Sleeps: A Deep Dive into Real-Time Engineering at Global Scale ### A beginner-friendly guide to the distributed systems, geospatial magic, and reliability engineering that power millions of rides every day.

Home » Articles » on Leadership & Career » ASQR&R » Robustness, Reliability and Quality. by John Martz Leave a Comment. # Robustness, Reliability and Quality. **Robustness:  That Often Overlooked Yet Powerful Discipline and Toolset.**Most companies have a Quality organization, and some have a Reliability organization. There are many ways to categorize the failures of your company’s products. It’s from these field failure categories that the need grew for the disciplines of Quality, Robustness and Reliability (with each discipline addressing the field failures of the corresponding color above):. **Reliability** – Product designed to last for the expected life for a given usage profile. **Robustness** – Product designed and manufactured to be insensitive to:. You can see from the definition of Robustness that if you made a product perfectly robust, you could address and eradicate all failures:  those spilling into the field from production, design life failures, and even wea- out failures. And the biggest driver for cost of ownership will be those failures occurring during the useful life of your product – that is, those failures occurring after the warranty period and prior to the end of life as the following illustrates:. Additionally, Robustness will address production and end-of-life failures along with quality and reliability, respectively, as the grayed-out areas of the bathtub curve depict. You can see from both the failures that Robustness tools address and the definition of Robustness that if you made a product perfectly robust, you could address and eradicate all failures:  those spilling into the field from production, design life failures, and wear-out issues. Here, I shared the causes of failure that Robustness tools can help with. In my next two articles, I’ll share specific tools of Reliability and Robustness and the advantages of using the two in concert. In that case, I recommend you investigate adding these tools to one of your existing groups — Quality, Reliability, or Design Engineering. Companies I’ve helped in the past have used these tools to address more failures than the tools of Quality and Reliability alone can address, and they’ve used them to outpace their competition. #### About John Martz. o Offering certifications for Applied Statistics, Quality and Reliability and Robustness (ASQR&R).

results.title: Design for Robustness and Reliability
results.content: # Design for Robustness and Reliability. In the field of engineering design, the concepts of robustness and reliability are paramount. The importance of designing for robustness and reliability cannot be overstated, as it directly impacts the safety, efficiency, and longevity of engineering solutions. * **Design of Experiments (DOE):** A statistical method that helps in understanding the influence of various factors on a system’s performance and identifying optimal conditions for robustness. The 1980s and 1990s witnessed the integration of computer-aided design (CAD) and computer-aided engineering (CAE) tools, which allowed for more sophisticated analysis and simulation of robustness and reliability. Designing for robustness and reliability has widespread applications across various industries. For instance, the design of jet engines incorporates redundancy and fault tolerance to ensure safe operation even in the event of component failures. The automotive industry relies heavily on robust and reliable designs to ensure vehicle safety and performance. Case studies have shown that implementing FMEA and DOE techniques in automotive design can significantly reduce the likelihood of failures and improve overall vehicle reliability. In the electronics industry, the miniaturization of components and the increasing complexity of circuits necessitate robust design practices. Robust design principles are applied to develop devices that can operate reliably under various physiological conditions. Despite the advancements in designing for robustness and reliability, several challenges remain:. Implementing robust and reliable design practices can be costly, particularly in the early stages of development. Designing for robustness and reliability is a critical aspect of engineering design that ensures systems and products perform consistently and safely under various conditions. The principles of robustness and reliability have evolved over time, driven by advancements in technology and the increasing complexity of engineering systems. Advanced topics like probabilistic design, reliability-centered maintenance, and robust optimization offer new avenues for enhancing system performance and dependability. However, challenges such as complexity, cost, data availability, and human factors must be addressed to fully realize the benefits of robust and reliable design. In conclusion, the importance of designing for robustness and reliability in engineering design cannot be overstated. As technology continues to advance, the field of robustness and reliability will undoubtedly play a crucial role in shaping the future of engineering design.

results.title: Sasol Governance of Ethics | SASOL GOVERNANCE OF ETHICS
results.content:
Title: Sasol Governance of Ethics | SASOL GOVERNANCE OF ETHICS
* Contact The Sasol Group Ethics Office. # Sasol Governance of Ethics. # Sasol Governance of Ethics. # Sasol Governance of Ethics. # SASOL GOVERNANCE OF ETHICS. The Sasol Limited Board of Directors is ultimately accountable for ethical business conduct in Sasol and to oversee ethical behaviour in accordance with the Sasol Code of Conduct. The Board has mandated the Safety, Social and Ethics Committee (SSEC) of the Board to ensure that Sasol has effective ethics policies, structures and programmes to institutionalise and monitor ethics in the company. In order to provide execution capability and capacity to the tasks of setting and achieving ethical objectives, advancing an ethical culture and addressing ethics risks and opportunities, The GEC appointed the Group Ethics Office (GEO), headed by the Chief Ethics Officer, as a functionally independent office that is the custodian of a comprehensive and integrated ethics programme. * Be the custodian of Sasol’s code of conduct, ethics strategy and ethics programme;. * provide ethics assurance and governance for Sasol. In order to provide execution capability and capacity to the tasks of setting and achieving ethical objectives, advancing an ethical culture and addressing ethics risks and opportunities, The GEC appointed the Group Ethics Office (GEO), headed by the Chief Ethics Officer, as a functionally independent office that is the custodian of a comprehensive and integrated ethics programme. * Be the custodian of Sasol’s code of conduct, ethics strategy and ethics programme;. Senior Vice Presidents (SVPs) and Vice Presidents (VPs) of the various Sasol business entities are accountable to their Executive Vice Presidents (EVP) for the implementation of the Sasol Code of Conduct and related policies in their businesses and are assisted by Ethics Officers that they have appointed for their respective entities. The Chief Ethics Officer, however, has the authority to raise matters of concern to the chair of the Sasol Audit Committee, chair of the SSCE Committee or the Chairman of the Board – without approval or fear of reprisal from the CEO, the Executive Vice President: Commercial and Legal, the Senior Vice President: Legal, Intellectual Property and Compliance, or any other senior manager, if so required by a situation.
